title: fix: stop Grafana denying dashboards for a minute after boot
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Every production deploy restarts Grafana with an empty database. The first authenticated request fills Grafana's 60s RBAC permission cache before the dashboards are provisioned, so for the next minute every Editor gets "Access denied to this dashboard" even though search still lists it. That is what Thomas hit right after the 25 Sep deploy.

- Fix: set `GF_RBAC_PERMISSION_CACHE=false` so permissions are read from Grafana's DB per request (a handful of admin users, negligible cost)
- Reproduced twice with `grafana/grafana:11.4.0`, the production auth proxy env and this repo's provisioning: 403 for exactly 60s after boot, then 200
- With the cache off: under a second of 404 while dashboards provision, then 200, no 403 window
- Observability tests pass; no change to auth or the admin gate

gist.headline: No more dashboard sulking
gist.blurb: Grafana now waits politely for its dashboards instead of remembering an empty room for a full minute. Editors can get back to watching the hive without the post-deploy cold shoulder.
gist.summary: Disabled Grafana's 60-second RBAC permission cache via `GF_RBAC_PERMISSION_CACHE=false`, preventing authenticated Editors from receiving dashboard 403s after production boot while provisioning completes.
gist.impact: After deploys, dashboard access now moves from a sub-second provisioning 404 to normal 200 responses, without the previous one-minute "Access denied" window for Editors.
